title: How CD Lasers Read Data

scenes.text: What wavelength lets a CD laser read tiny pits?
It uses an infrared laser at roughly 780 nanometers.
scenes.label: 780 NM INFRARED

scenes.text: The beam reflects off the disc’s aluminum layer, differing on pits vs. lands.
scenes.label: ALUMINUM REFLECTION
scenes.query: CD aluminum layer reflection pits lands

scenes.text: A photodiode converts the reflected light variations into digital signals.
scenes.label: PHOTODIODE SIGNAL
scenes.query: CD photodiode converts light to data

scenes.text: Follow for the future, one byte at a time.

description: Three precise steps a CD player takes to turn tiny pits into music and data. Stay tuned for more easy tech breakdowns.
